(user)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser

It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research

If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

(claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: backlink-dach
commands.description: Run the 741 Backlink Workflow DACH for a local business — competitor backlink analysis, free niche-directory research, local ecosystem outreach (Verbände, Vereine, Hersteller), digital PR, and a strict backlink-buy path. Produces a scored target list in a Google Sheet with per-row approval checkboxes. Trigger on "Backlink-Workflow für <Kunde>", "Linkaufbau für <Kunde>", "run the backlink workflow", or when Martin names a client, city and budget and says "go" for this workflow. Do NOT use for citation/NAP directory work (that is the Citations module, this workflow only owns the free niche-directory research within it) and do NOT use for the CRO homepage prototype (use cro-homepage). (user)

commands.name: behandler-seite
commands.description: Baue eine E-E-A-T-Behandler-Seite (Über-mich/Practitioner-Trust-Page) für einen Health-Kunden von 741 — mit Person-Schema, sameAs, HWG-sicheren Texten und Vorschau-Deploy. Nutzen bei "Behandlerseite", "Über-mich-Seite aufbauen", "practitioner page", "E-E-A-T Seite" für Heilpraktiker/Ärzte/Therapeuten/Coaches im Gesundheitsbereich. (user)

commands.name: client-access-lockout
commands.description: Handles the case where a 741 program client removes or restricts our access to a tool or account (Search Console, WordPress, Google profile, ads, any login) out of worry or mistrust. Verifies every claim with live data, cross-checks our own "done" statuses, builds an internal dossier, a client-ready work overview and a calm reply in Martin's voice, and tracks the follow-up stages. Use when Martin says "sie hat uns rausgeworfen", "hat uns gekickt", "Zugang entzogen", "Zugriff eingeschränkt", or pastes a client message that restricts access. Do NOT use when the client only criticises or asks a question without removing access, or for a routine status question ("warum ist X noch nicht fertig") — that is a normal reply. (user)

commands.name: content-writing
commands.description: Write finished website copy for a 741 client or for 741.studio. New pages (homepage, service, location, practitioner, cost, FAQ) and blog posts, or a rewrite of an existing page. Builds a brief from the content pool, runs the A0 gate, writes an outline for Martin's go, drafts, runs scripted gates for facts, HWG/BRAO, SEO, style and AI slop (German tell list plus rival-model cleanse), has a fresh reviewer check it, and delivers a Markdown master with section IDs and CMS plain-text blocks. Use on "/content-write <client> <page or topic>", "schreib die Seite für …", "Blogbeitrag für …", "Text für die Ortsseite …", "Seitentext überarbeiten". Do NOT use for the content pool (content-pool), for auditing a page (seo-page-optimizer AUDIT), for the CRO prototype (cro-homepage), for prospect review pages (local-seo-review-page), or for social posts and emails. (user)

commands.name: cro-homepage
commands.description: Run the 741 CRO Homepage Workflow (Track A, the standard) for a local business: healing practices (Heilpraktiker, Physio), law firms and other local companies. Turns the current homepage or one page of a client into an approved, conversion-optimised desktop HTML prototype with a GPT mockup, a Chrome visual check, a handoff and a Drive folder. Trigger on "CRO homepage for <name>", "run the CRO workflow", "Startseite optimieren (CRO)", "homepage prototype for <practice>", "prototype for <firm>", or Martin naming a client with the URL and saying go. Do NOT use for Track B design-intense runs ("track B", showpiece, motion-heavy pitch), SEO content specs (seo-page-optimizer), review pages (local-seo-review-page), backlink work (backlink-dach), or copy for one practitioner page without a prototype (behandler-seite). (user)

commands.name: morning-grill
commands.description: Runs the 741 morning grill and evening log for all clients. Morning - scans what happened since the last grill (chats, registry, git in all worktrees, portal standup, night shift, citations, calendar, goal sheet), builds max 7 ranked decision cards and a one-page brief, grills Martin with clickable cards, then writes today's plan per client with owner (Martin, Dinakar, Tantri, Gayo, agent). Evening - drafts done / open / tomorrow / blockers per client for Martin to confirm. Use when Martin says "grill me", "morning grill", "Morgen-Grill", "was steht heute an", "daily brief for the clients", "log the day", "Tagesabschluss", or when the 06:00 / 17:00 scheduled task fires. Do NOT use for one client's deep work (use that client's chat or workflow), for the 741 news brief (daily-brief), or for Martin's personal mood check-in (daily-checkin). (user)

commands.name: local-seo-review-page

commands.name: night-shift
commands.description: Autonomous overnight run for the 741 local-SEO program. Reads the open content tasks of running client programs from the portal, produces page content specs (CREATE) and page audits (AUDIT) with the seo-page-optimizer standard, verifies each result with a Critic, and stages everything as Markdown drafts for the morning review. Use this whenever the task is about page content, on-page SEO, "optimise this page", "write the [service] page", "topical authority", "rank in AI / ChatGPT / AI Overviews / Perplexity", "GEO", "AEO", "content brief", or checking whether an existing page is aligned with our SEO standard — for any 741 local-SEO client (Hüwel, Suriya/Coralie, Dumann, Kamil, Brasse, etc.). For the prospect Maps-grid audit deliverable use `local-seo-review-page` instead; this skill is about the CONTENT of a page. (project)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory

commands.name: morning

Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf

Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

305	   thumbnail appears, the upload silently failed, re-find the attach button fresh and
306	   retry rather than typing into a broken composer. **Attach both the practitioner
307	   reference photos AND the real logo files** (icon + wordmark from `01-input/`), not
308	   photos alone. Say so explicitly in the prompt text, e.g. "the attached logo files
309	   are the real brand logo, reproduce this exact logo in the header, do not invent a
310	   different one." Without this the model draws its own invented logo text instead of
311	   the client's real mark (seen on the Dumann run, fixed from the next run on).
312	3. Set image effort to **High** (the effort slider next to the model row).
313	4. Type **one single message with everything in it**, as one block with no blank-line
314	   paragraph breaks (a literal blank line in this composer can submit the message
315	   early, mid-type, while a response is already streaming): the global style block
316	   (colours, fonts, mood, layout pattern), AND every section's exact headline, body
317	   text, CTA label, FAQ question and answer, review quote, in full, not shortened,
318	   taken verbatim from `approved-copy.md`. This is the same content that used to be
319	   split into "design doc" and "copy", sent together in one go.
320	5. Verify with a screenshot that the composer shows the full text intact and the
321	   photos are still attached, then click the send button explicitly (do not rely on
322	   the Enter key for a long multi-paragraph message).
323	6. Wait for completion (High effort takes 1–2 minutes on a 10-section page). Open the
324	   full image in the lightbox and download it from there.
325	7. Download to `06-gpt-assets/`, named `full-page-v<n>-final.png` once approved.
326	
327	**Drive upload, mandatory step (Martin, 2026-10-11): the final approved GPT image
328	always goes into the client's Drive CRO folder, every run, not just on request.**
329	Do this through the visual browser (Claude in Chrome). **Never use the Drive MCP
330	tool for images or any binary file** — it needs the full content inline as one
331	literal parameter value, which is impractical past a few hundred KB. The MCP tool
332	stays for the markdown work docs only (rule 2.2).
333	
334	**Tested, working procedure for the browser upload (2026-10-11):** clicking Drive's
335	"File upload" menu item with a normal trusted click opens a native macOS file picker
336	that no tool can see or interact with — don't do that. Instead:
337	
338	1. Open the Drive folder, click "New" to open the menu.
339	2. Run a JavaScript click on the menu item instead of a real mouse click:
340	   `[...document.querySelectorAll('[role=menuitem]')].find(e =>
341	   e.innerText.trim().startsWith('File upload')).click()`. An untrusted,
342	   script-dispatched click cannot open the native OS picker (browsers block that for
343	   security), but it still makes Drive create its real `<input type="file">` in the
344	   DOM and does not block anything.
345	3. `find` with a query like "hidden file input element" to get that input's ref
346	   (it only exists after step 2, there is none on the page before).
347	4. Call `file_upload` with that ref and the local file path. Drive's own "Uploading…"
348	   toast appears and the file lands in the current folder, confirmed by a green
349	   "upload complete" checkmark.
350	5. If step 2 or 3 ever stops finding the input (Google can change this), fall back to
351	   delivering the file to Martin with `SendUserFile` and naming the Drive folder, but
352	   try the steps above first — they are the real, working path, not a last resort.
353	
354	**Learnings from the Dumann run (2026-10-11):**
355	- A multi-paragraph `type` action with blank lines between sections can trigger an
356	  early send after the first paragraph in this composer; the rest of the text then
357	  sits unsent in the box. Avoid blank lines in the typed message, or verify with a
358	  screenshot before sending.
359	- ChatGPT's chained "edit this image" follow-ups in the same thread (recognisable by
360	  "Interpreted the edit" appearing above the generation) have repeatedly stalled at
361	  95–98% and self-cancelled ("Image generation stopped"), even after "Try again". A
362	  fresh, complete, single-message generation in a new chat does not have this problem
363	  and should be preferred over iterative follow-ups.
364	- A very long prompt (about 12,000 characters, whole page copy) typed with the `type` action makes the page busy for about 1 to 2 minutes, and the tool reports a timeout and screenshots fail meanwhile. The typing still completes. Wait, then check with `javascript_tool` that the composer text length equals the prompt length and ends with the last words (`document.querySelector('#prompt-textarea').innerText`). Then find the Send button with `find` and click it. Do not retype.
365	- **Fast prompt insertion (2026-10-10, tested):** write the prompt to a file, run `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 pbcopy < prompt.txt`, click the composer, press `cmd+v`. ChatGPT turns a long paste (about 15,000 characters) into a chip "Pasted text" within seconds, no freeze. Click "Show in text field" on the chip, then check the length with `javascript_tool` (`document.querySelector('#prompt-textarea').innerText.length` must equal the file length), then find the Send button and click it. This replaces the slow `type` action.
366	- The "+" menu's "Add photos & files" item can trigger a native OS file picker that
367	  the agent cannot see or interact with; use the dedicated "Attach photos" file input
368	  instead, found fresh via `find` right before uploading (a stale element reference
369	  from an earlier screenshot can silently fail to attach).
370	
371	Martin decided (2026-10-11) that once the brief is solid, one good full-page image is
372	enough and needs no separate approval round, the agent proceeds straight to Step 6. Status
373	goes to `Bilder freigegeben` and the build uses the image only as a layout/style reference,
374	never as a copy source, the approved copy stays the source of truth for every word on the
375	prototype.
376	
377	**Standing rule (Martin, 2026-10-11): the single GPT prompt carries the FULL content of
378	`approved-copy.md`, not a shortened version.** Every headline, every body paragraph, every
379	step description, every FAQ question AND its answer, every review quote in full, the full
380	address block, all nine sections in full text, not abbreviated labels. The goal is one
381	image that is as close as possible to the finished page, generated once, with no
382	in-between draft rounds and no section-by-section pass. If the first image still misses
383	real content, the fix is a fuller prompt, not a second round of smaller images.
384	
385	### Step 5b — High-resolution image assets → `06-gpt-assets/images/` → no checkpoint
386	
387	**Why (Martin, 2026-10-11):** crops cut out of the full-page mockup are only about 100 to 330 px wide and look soft when the prototype shows them larger. The mockup is the design reference, not the image source.
388	
389	Run this after the final mockup exists:
390	
391	1. **Read the final mockup in detail and list every image slot (Martin, 2026-10-11).** Open the final mockup at full size and zoom into each section. Write `06-gpt-assets/images/SLOTS.md` with one row per image the prototype must show: section number, what the picture shows, shape and display size at 1440 px (for example 480×320 card), and the decision. The decision is one of three:
392	   - **Real:** a photo from `01-input/` fits the slot in subject, colour and light. Use it, even if the mockup shows a different picture. A real photo that clashes with the other images (for example a cold blue photo among warm ones) does not fit: choose Regenerate.
393	   - **Regenerate:** no real photo fits. Make a clean high-resolution version of what the mockup shows (step 2).
394	   - **None:** the slot is a logo, icon or text. Use the real logo file or live HTML.
395	   Include the hero portrait, card photos, second portraits, room or entrance photos, and decorative botanicals or icons. A slot missing from the list will later show a soft crop, so check the list against every section of the mockup before you go on.
396	   **Gate:** the prototype build (Step 6) does not start until every slot has a file in `06-gpt-assets/images/` or `01-input/` and a row in SLOTS.md.
397	2. **One fresh chat per image.** Never a follow-up in the mockup thread: edit follow-ups stall at 95 to 98 percent (see Step 5 learnings). Attach the final mockup (it shows style and slot), the practitioner reference photos if she appears in the image, and the logo only if it appears. Send one single message: the subject of this one image, "same style, light and colours as the attached mockup", the practitioner likeness rule if she appears, "photograph only, no text, no UI, no logo, no frame", the format (landscape 1536×1024 for card and wide images, portrait 1024×1536 for portraits, square 1024×1024 for icons and textures), High effort.
398	3. **Download each from the lightbox** and name it `06-gpt-assets/images/<nn>-<section>-<subject>.png`, with `<nn>` the section number in the mockup. Open every file and check it: the long edge is at least 1024 px and the content is right.
399	4. **Size rule:** a prototype image must be at least the size it is shown at on a 1440 px screen. A GPT image at 1024 px or more satisfies this for card and portrait slots.
400	5. **Run several chats at once:** one browser tab per image, up to three at a time, is faster and works. If an upload to the composer fails with a lost connection, find the file input again and upload again, then check that the thumbnail shows before sending. After the download, copy (never move) the file into `06-gpt-assets/images/`.
401	   **Likeness when the only real photo is unusable (2026-10-10):** if the real photo hides the face (sunglasses) or is a private holiday photo, attach the final mockup first (its person is the face of the page) and the real photo second as reference for hair, build and skin tone. Write "she must NOT wear sunglasses". Every person image of the page then shows the same woman as the mockup. Record in the handoff that the face is invented and a real portrait is needed.
402	6. **Upload** the finished files to the client's Drive CRO folder with the browser method in Step 5. The browser upload accepts about 10 MB per call, so send large sets in two calls.
403	7. **Shoot list:** every generated image that shows the practitioner or the practice goes on the handoff shoot list, so the client can replace it with a real photo later.
404	
405	### Step 6 — HTML prototype → `07-prototype/index.html` (a rebuild goes to `07-prototype/v2/`, never overwrite) → **Checkpoint 2**
406	
407	**Desktop only (Martin, 2026-10-11).** The workflow starts from the desktop mockup, so the prototype is a desktop build at 1440 px that matches the mockup as closely as possible. A mobile version is not part of this workflow; it belongs to the later rebuild workflow and goes on the handoff as an open item.
408	
409	Inputs: the GPT mockup as layout and style reference; `approved-copy.md` as exact text; `brand.md` as design system; **`00_project/cro-homepage-motion-spec.md` as the fixed motion and highlight spec (Martin, 2026-10-11)**; the real logo files and real photos from `01-input/`; the high-resolution images from `06-gpt-assets/images/` (Step 5b). Never use crops of the mockup as page images.
410	
411	1. **Desktop 1440 px:**
412	   - primary CTA visible in the first screen;
413	   - body text at least 16 px.
414	2. **Rebuild each section** to match the mockup section by section (layout, spacing, proportions, colours), with live text. No text baked into images.
415	3. **Motion:** build exactly the spec: one highlight per section, calm reveal once, breathing CTA in hero and closer only, reduced-motion respected, nothing from the spec's "does not move" list.
416	4. **Clickable:** CTAs open the client's primary channel (`wa.me/<number>?text=<prefill>` for WhatsApp, the booking link for a booking form, `tel:` for phone); service cards link to `#` placeholders; FAQ uses accordions.
417	5. **Logo is always the real file** from `01-input/`. Real photos are used wherever they match; Step 5b images fill the gaps and are on the shoot list.
418	6. **Anything not in the approved copy stays visibly flagged** (`[FEHLT]` badge in the page and in `self-check.md`), never silently filled in.
419	7. **Build the `?shot=1` mode** (shows all reveal states) for headless screenshots at 1440 px. These screenshots are for the record. They do not replace the visual check in Step 6b. Compare each section with the mockup side by side and note differences. Save the screenshots to `07-prototype/screenshots/`.
420	
421	**Step 6b — Visual check in Chrome (mandatory, Martin 2026-10-11).** Before the self-check and before any report that the prototype is done, the agent opens the prototype in Claude in Chrome, scrolls it from top to bottom at 1440×900, and checks every item in `00_project/cro-homepage-visual-check.md`: measured checks, global visual items, per-section items, and interaction checks. Everything found wrong is fixed and checked again. The result goes to `07-prototype/visual-check.md`. The agent may not write "done" or "ready for Checkpoint 2" without the line "Visual check done in Chrome, N items checked, N fixed, N open". This applies to every prototype build and every later change to the prototype.
422	
423	**Self-check → `07-prototype/self-check.md`:** re-score the prototype with `scorecard.md`. Pass condition: every Priority A item scores 2, and all "Done" conditions from section 0 hold. If it fails, fix and re-run. No checkpoint before the check passes.
424	
425	**Gate for Checkpoint 2:** `visual-check.md` exists and has no open item that the agent could fix. Open items that need client data are listed as `[FEHLT]`.
426	
427	**Checkpoint 2 — Martin approves the prototype.** Approved → status `Prototyp freigegeben`, go to Step 7. This is the only remaining checkpoint after copy, since the design doc and the GPT image round both run without a stop now.
428	
429	**Build learnings (Dumann run, 2026-10-11):**
430	- Cut out portraits with the `rembg` Python API (`new_session('u2net')`, `alpha_matting=True`), not the `rembg` command line, which fails on a missing `watchdog` module. Run it with the Python that has `rembg` installed (`/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.10/bin/python3` on this Mac).
431	- Cut an icon sheet apart by labelling the non-white regions (scipy). Make the white background transparent by flood fill from the border, then blur the alpha by 1 px. A white box shows around icons on white cards otherwise.
432	- A line drawing on a solid purple image goes onto a band of nearly the same purple with `mix-blend-mode: lighten`. Do not use `screen`, it brightens the whole rectangle.
433	- A real photo cut out at the image edge shows a hard edge. Fade that side with a CSS `mask-image` gradient.
434	- A cutout has a pale fringe from the old backdrop. Fix it by edge unmixing: for every semi-transparent pixel, subtract the known backdrop colour (taken from the nearest fully transparent pixel of the source photo) and divide by the alpha. Do not fill edge pixels with the nearest solid colour: that makes blocky hair. Check the result on the real band colour at 100 percent.
435	- Always set `height:auto` on an `<img>` that has `width:100%` in CSS. A leftover `height` attribute stretches the picture (found on the about portrait; measured by M4b).
436	- Turn automatic hyphenation off in narrow cards (`hyphens:manual`). For one unavoidable long German word add a soft hyphen (`­`) at the compound break.
437	- A portrait on a 3:2 card is cropped from the top of the original, with the hairline visible. Check the crop at card size.
438	- Serve the folder with `python3 -m http.server <port>` for the live check. Port 8765 can be taken by an older process. Check with `curl` first.
439	
440	**Build learnings (law firm run, 2026-10-10):**
441	- Chrome's real viewport is about 1440×757 (sometimes 1421×701 with scrollbar). The first screen must hold H1, one proof line and the CTA at **701 px height**. Put the rating line between the sub-headline and the buttons so proof and CTA are visible together. Check `getBoundingClientRect().bottom` of the CTA.
442	- A hero with three buttons or a long label wraps in a 700 px column. Use `flex-wrap:nowrap`, drop the arrow icon in the hero button and set padding to 24 px.
443	- `text-wrap: balance` on all headings removes single-word last lines.
444	- A fixed side rail with dark buttons vanishes on a dark band. Give the buttons a 2 px ring in the page colour.
445	- A "grey to ink while scrolling" paragraph: wrap each word, lighten words with `opacity` as a function of scroll position, never darken them again. Make the formula reach 100 percent while the paragraph is still well inside the screen.
446	- A hand-drawn wave under a headline line: a `::after` with a repeating SVG background, `transform: scaleX(0)` to `1` once on load. `white-space:nowrap` on the line, otherwise the wave stretches over the wrapped box.
447	- Numbers of the type 01, 02, 03 in stacked service rows keep links on one line when the item is a flex column and the link has `margin-top:auto`.
448	- Text check by script (M11): parse the HTML text nodes, normalise, and test each against the normalised `approved-copy.md`. Expect only the prototype notice to differ.
449	
450	### Step 7 — Handoff package → `08-handoff/handoff.md`
451	
452	For the separate rebuild workflow:
453	
454	1. Path to the prototype, the design doc and the GPT assets.
455	2. `approved-copy.md` with title, description, H1.
456	3. Image assets plus shoot list for missing real photos.
457	4. Tracking spec for the client's primary channel: event `whatsapp_click` on every wa.me link, or `booking_click` on every booking link, or `phone_click` on every tel link, each with a `section` parameter. For WhatsApp also the prefilled message per section. Setup itself is not part of this workflow.
458	5. `[FEHLT]` list: every fact Martin must get from the client before go-live.
459	6. Before/after score table.
460	7. Learnings entry appended to `rules.md`.
461	
462	**The final report always carries the direct link to the client's Drive folder of the run (Martin, 2026-10-11), and the full-page screenshot of the prototype sent as a file, so Martin can open the result at once.** **Register (Martin, 2026-10-11, updated):** after every new page and every new prototype version, add or update the entry in `00_project/cro-registry/registry.json` (fields as in the existing entries, `approved: false`) and run `python3 00_project/cro-registry/build.py`. It rebuilds `~/Desktop/Workflow-Uebersicht.xlsx` for all workflows (sheets Übersicht, Links, Workflows; plain-text links, no hyperlink objects). When Martin approves a prototype: `python3 00_project/workflow-registry/workflow_registry.py approve --cro-id <id>` in the same turn. Keep the sheet simple. Prototypes are opened locally as files, never uploaded to a server unasked. Status → `Übergeben`. Last action of the run: mirror the whole run to the Drive folder as described in 2.2 (all documents in current version, all images, the prototype zip, the final screenshots, `_status.md`), and check the folder listing against the local folder.
463	
464	---
465	
466	## 4b. Other page types (first used for the Über-mich page, 2026-10-11)
467	
468	The same steps run for a single other page of the same client, for example a practitioner page ("Über mich"). Apply these differences. Everything else stays as written.
469	
470	1. **Folders.** Local `00_project/assets/<slug>/cro/<page-slug>/` with the same subfolders (01 to 08, plus `_status.md` and `00-lead-info.md`). Drive: a subfolder `<Seitenname>` inside the client's `CRO Homepage` folder, with the same upload rules as section 2.2. The client's assets and brand are shared: link to `../01-input/` and `../02-data/brand.md`, do not copy them again. The design system and reusable assets of the finished homepage prototype are the base for the build.
471	2. **Step 1 data.** Scrape the current page and every page it links to for facts (qualifications, memberships, teaching, location, history). Keep the exact wording with its source URL. Record a table of conflicts and compliance findings (for example a fact that differs between two pages, or a sentence with a healing claim). Use only the newer and safer statement on the new page and write the conflict in `[FEHLT]` and in the handoff. Check the technical state of the current page: schema, title, H1, headings, alt texts.
472	3. **Step 2 scorecard.** Skip scorecard items that only belong to entry pages (sub-headline with the situation, first-appointment section, situations section, service cards). Add the items of the page type. For a practitioner page: A1 name, role and city in title, H1 and meta; A2 Person schema; A3 career is proven and readable. Plan the sections from the proven pattern of the page type (skill `behandler-seite` and library pattern P1) and run the coverage check against the 10 rows of the P0 blueprint with a reason for every row left out.
473	4. **Step 3 copy.** Same rules. For health clients add the mandatory notice box. Rewrite any personal story so that it states the motivation and no treatment result. Every quoted text in the final prompt must be found in `approved-copy.md` (check by script before sending).
474	5. **Step 5 mockup.** Attach the finished homepage mockup as style reference, so both pages look like one website. If the page needs photos of the person at work, plan them as photo slots in the mockup. Generate them later with the portraits attached as the face reference (Step 5b) and put them on the shoot list.
475	6. **Step 6 prototype.** Add the schema of the page type as valid JSON-LD in the head (for a practitioner page a Person with credentials, work place and expertise). Leave `sameAs` empty until verified profiles exist. Add `noindex,nofollow` while the page is a preview.
476	7. **Step 7 handoff.** Add: the new URL and the redirect from the old URL, the menu and internal links that must point to the new page, and any correction the new facts force on other pages (for example a statement on the homepage that the new data proves outdated).
477	
478	## 5. Templates
479	
480	**`_status.md` line:**
481	
482	```
483	2026-10-11 · Step 1 done · 02-data/dataset.md · next: Step 2
484	```
485	
486	**`00-lead-info.md`:**
487	
488	```markdown
489	# <Praxis> — Lead-Info
490	Praxis: · Behandler/in: · Website: · CMS: · GBP: · Kontaktkanal (WhatsApp, Telefon oder Buchungsformular): · Quelle: · Status: Lead
491	```
492	
493	**Scorecard row (`scorecard.md`):**
494	
495	| # | Regel | Prüfung | Prio | Score 0/1/2 | Beleg |
496	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
497	| 1 | Hero nennt das Problem des Besuchers und die Stadt | H1 + Subline lesen | A |  |  |
498	| 2 | Primärer CTA im ersten Bildschirm sichtbar | Screenshot 1440 px | A |  |  |
499	| 3 | Gesicht und Qualifikation der Behandlerin above the fold oder in Sektion 2 | Screenshot | A |  |  |
500	| … | 15–25 Items aus der CRO-Library |  |  |  |  |
501	
502	**GPT section prompt skeleton:**
503	
504	```
505	[GLOBAL STYLE BLOCK]
506	Sektion <n> — <Name>. Layout: <Pattern aus patterns.md>.
507	Headline (exakt): "…" · CTA (exakt): "…"
508	Echtes Foto: <Beschreibung + Position> · Hintergrund: … · Textur: … · Abstand: …
509	Format: Hochformat 1024×1536. Look der echten Praxis (Referenzfotos anhängen). Eine CTA-Farbe.
510	```
511	
512	---
513	
514	## 6. Decisions on the open points
515	
516	| # | Point | Decision (Martin, 2026-10-11) |
517	| --- | --- | --- |
518	| 1 | Claude Design or HTML | HTML only |
519	| 2 | Browser for ChatGPT | Claude in Chrome, Martin's logged-in session; portrait 1024×1536 per section |
520	| 3 | NotebookLM export | one time, done now, into `00_project/knowledge/cro-library/` |
521	| 4 | Drive folder | `Local SEO/<Name>/CRO Homepage/` |
522	| 5 | Contact channel | asked per client before the run; not always WhatsApp |
523	| 6 | Existing homepage text | used as input when one exists |
524	| 7 | Images | real photos as reference, GPT creates the ideal images for the prototype |
525	| 8 | Pass condition | all Priority A = 2, all Done conditions (default kept) |
526	| 9 | Skill location | `~/.claude/skills/cro-homepage/SKILL.md` (default kept) |
527	
528	---
529	
530	## 7. Sequence of first use
531	
532	1. ~~Agent exports the NotebookLM notebook and derives `rules.md`, `patterns.md`, `scorecard.md`.~~ Done and approved 2026-10-11.
533	2. ~~Agent writes the skill `cro-homepage`.~~ Done 2026-10-11.
534	3. Martin names the practice, the URL, the GBP link and the preferred contact channel, and says "go". Agent runs Step 0 to Checkpoint 1. No pilot is set yet.
535	
536	## Registry: automatic (2026-10-11)
537	
538	The overview Excel `~/Desktop/Workflow-Uebersicht.xlsx` updates itself. A Stop hook runs `workflow_registry.py sync --quiet` after every turn. You do not call `upsert` for normal progress. Step 7 writes the line `Step 7 done` into `_status.md` of the page folder. `sync` then shows the page as fertig, Freigabe offen. Pages that already have an entry in `cro-registry/registry.json` stay manual (approval, version, archive).
539	For any other file layout, write `_run.json` in the run folder (schema in `00_project/workflow-registry/README.md`). Only the approval stays manual: when Martin approves a result, run `approve` in the same turn and say that the Excel is updated.
540	
541	## Martin guide (2026-10-12)
542	
543	The 741 character Martin points out the one thing per section the reader must not miss. Rules, poses, markup and the inline helper: `00_project/assets/brand/martin-guide/README.md`. In this workflow: only in the presentation wrapper around the prototype (insight next to the change rationale). Never inside the prototype markup. Max 1 callout per section, bubble text in first person and plain language, every number with source and date, check desktop and mobile with a screenshot.

## 0. Purpose and outcome

The workflow turns the current homepage of a local healing practice into an approved, optimised homepage prototype. The prototype is built to turn local visitors into WhatsApp contacts. It is a sales artifact for leads and a bonus for clients. It is not a paid deliverable for now.

The output is a clickable HTML prototype plus a handoff package. The rebuild of the live site runs in a separate workflow.

**Done (all must be true):**

1. Every scorecard item is scored 2, or has a written reason why it does not apply.
2. On a 1440 px desktop viewport, the primary CTA is visible in the first screen without scrolling.
3. The CTA repeats at least every 2 sections.
4. The first 3 sections answer: who it is for, what helps, how the first visit works, where the practice is, why to trust the practitioner.
5. Every claim, price and credential traces to `02-data/dataset.md`. Nothing is invented. Gaps carry the flag `[FEHLT]`.
6. Zero healing promises. The HWG check passed.
7. Martin approved all 3 checkpoints.

1. Martin triggers a run with: practice name, website URL, GBP link, and the preferred contact channel of the practice (WhatsApp, phone, booking form). The channel is asked per client before the run. It is not always WhatsApp. The doc says "WhatsApp" as the default example.

3. Tools: Firecrawl (scrape, screenshots), Claude in Chrome (screenshots, GBP read-out), DataForSEO (keywords), Google Search Console and GA4 via the 741 service account where 741 holds access, Google Drive MCP (work docs), Claude in Chrome (ChatGPT image generation, NotebookLM export). 10. **Industry mode.** The workflow is built for local healing practices first, but it works for any local business. Health practices run in HWG mode: no healing promises, no before/after, no fear wording (rules L8/L9, scorecard item 22). Other industries skip the HWG items. Result claims are then allowed when the dataset backs them with real data.
    **Lawyers (law firms):** scorecard item 22 becomes the **Anwaltswerbe-Check** (BRAO § 43b, BORA § 6, UWG). ### Step 2 — Diagnosis and ideal outcome → `03-diagnosis/diagnosis.md`

Pool input (row 1.0): `content-pool/04-pool/pool-top.md` lists the content items per CRO row, best first (A, B, C), with the `[FEHLT]` facts and the HWG notes. Use it when you write the one line per section in item 4. Items with the status `needs_client` stay drafts. The pool never removes one of the 10 rows. The sitemap is a separate output of the content pool and is not an input here.

1. **Score the current homepage** with `scorecard.md`. Each item gets 0, 1 or 2 plus one line of evidence (quote, screenshot name, number).
2. **List the gaps:** every item with 0 or 1.
3. **Rank the fixes** by impact on contacts through the client's primary channel (WhatsApp, phone or booking form):
   - Priority A: hero, CTA, first-visit clarity, trust above the fold.
   - Priority B: proof, offer, location.
   - Priority C: everything else.
4. **Ideal-outcome plan:** pick the layout pattern from `patterns.md` that fits the brand. Write the target section order with one line per section on its job. **Default order is the full P0 blueprint from `patterns.md`, 10 sections, not a shortened list:**
   1. Hero: visitor's problem and outcome, city, practitioner photo, primary CTA, Google rating.
   2. Beweis-Leiste: a second, short proof placement right after the hero (big rating, one highlighted quote), separate from the full review section lower down. This row is the one most often dropped, it does not repeat, it is a compact appetiser for the full review wall in row 7.
   3. "Ist das etwas für mich?": 3–5 complaints the practice works with.
   4. Leistungen: cards, each linked to its service page.
   5. Der erste Termin: 3–4 steps, duration, price.
   6. Über die Behandlerin: photo, credentials, why she does this work.
   7. Bewertungen: Google rating and selected reviews, within HWG limits.
   8. FAQ: Kosten, Krankenkasse, Vorbereitung, Absage.
   9. Standort: map, address, parking, hours.
   10. Abschluss-CTA: primary channel, phone as secondary.
5. **Fact gaps:** every fact the plan needs but the dataset lacks → `[FEHLT: …]` list for Martin.

**Gate:** Every 0 or 1 score has an evidence line. Any score without evidence is redone. **Section-coverage check (Martin, 2026-10-11, added after a real miss on the Dumann run):** before Step 3 starts, the agent lists the 10 P0 rows from `patterns.md` against the ideal-outcome plan above, one line each, either "included as section N" or "deliberately dropped, reason: …" (a reason grounded in real data or the niche, e.g. "no comparison table, no real competitor data and a comparison reads as salesy for a solo practitioner"). A row silently missing, with no explicit drop reason, fails this gate and the plan is redone. This check is mandatory on every run, not a one-off fix.

- body copy;

### Step 4 — Design data and GPT design doc → `05-gpt-design-doc/design-doc.md` → no checkpoint

Runs straight through from the approved copy to the first GPT image. Martin decided (2026-10-11) that the design doc itself needs no separate approval; the first real checkpoint after copy is Checkpoint 2, once the GPT images exist.

Inputs: `approved-copy.md`, `brand.md`, the pattern chosen in Step 2.

**Doc structure:**

1. **Global style block** (pasted at the top of every GPT prompt): brand colours as hex, fonts, mood words, imagery style, chosen layout pattern, image format rules.
2. **One prompt per section**, in page order: layout pattern, exact headline and CTA text, where the real photo goes, background and texture, spacing.
3. **Full-page prompt:** the whole homepage as one tall reference image.
4. **Image rule:** the real photos are the reference. GPT creates the ideal images for the prototype, including people and rooms, in the look of the real practice. This is part of the improvement. The handoff lists a shoot list so the client can replace them with real photos later. Do-nots: no stock-photo look; no generated text as final copy; one CTA colour only.

### Step 5 — GPT image generation → `06-gpt-assets/` → no checkpoint

The agent runs ChatGPT through Claude in Chrome in Martin's logged-in session.

**Default (Martin, 2026-10-11): one full-page image, one message, done.** Generate the
whole homepage as one tall reference image from a single, complete prompt. No
section-by-section prompts, no draft rounds, no follow-up edit messages in the same
thread (ChatGPT's edit flow on a prior image has repeatedly stalled at 95–98% and
cancelled itself, see Learnings below). If a redo is needed, start a fresh chat and send
one new complete message, never a follow-up on the old one.

**Exact procedure, tested and confirmed working on the Dumann run:**

1. Start a **brand new chat** (full page navigation to `chatgpt.com`, not just the
   sidebar "New chat" button, which can leave a stale composer draft or land in "Work"
   mode instead of "Chat" mode — always check the top toggle shows "Chat" selected).
2. Attach the real reference images first (`Attach photos` in the composer), confirm
   with a screenshot that thumbnails actually appear before typing anything. If no
   thumbnail appears, the upload silently failed, re-find the attach button fresh and
   retry rather than typing into a broken composer. **Attach both the practitioner
   reference photos AND the real logo files** (icon + wordmark from `01-input/`), not
   photos alone. Say so explicitly in the prompt text, e.g. "the attached logo files
   are the real brand logo, reproduce this exact logo in the header, do not invent a
   different one." Without this the model draws its own invented logo text instead of
   the client's real mark (seen on the Dumann run, fixed from the next run on).
3. Set image effort to **High** (the effort slider next to the model row).
4. Type **one single message with everything in it**, as one block with no blank-line
   paragraph breaks (a literal blank line in this composer can submit the message
   early, mid-type, while a response is already streaming): the global style block
   (colours, fonts, mood, layout pattern), AND every section's exact headline, body
   text, CTA label, FAQ question and answer, review quote, in full, not shortened,
   taken verbatim from `approved-copy.md`. This is the same content that used to be
   split into "design doc" and "copy", sent together in one go.
5. Verify with a screenshot that the composer shows the full text intact and the
   photos are still attached, then click the send button explicitly (do not rely on
   the Enter key for a long multi-paragraph message).
6. Wait for completion (High effort takes 1–2 minutes on a 10-section page). Open the
   full image in the lightbox and download it from there.
7. Download to `06-gpt-assets/`, named `full-page-v<n>-final.png` once approved.

**Drive upload, mandatory step (Martin, 2026-10-11): the final approved GPT image
always goes into the client's Drive CRO folder, every run, not just on request.**

literal parameter value, which is impractical past a few hundred KB. The MCP tool
stays for the markdown work docs only (rule 2.2).

**Tested, working procedure for the browser upload (2026-10-11):** clicking Drive's
"File upload" menu item with a normal trusted click opens a native macOS file picker
that no tool can see or interact with — don't do that. Instead:

1. Open the Drive folder, click "New" to open the menu.
2. Run a JavaScript click on the menu item instead of a real mouse click:
   `[...document.querySelectorAll('[role=menuitem]')].find(e =>
   e.innerText.trim().startsWith('File upload')).click()`. An untrusted,
   script-dispatched click cannot open the native OS picker (browsers block that for
   security), but it still makes Drive create its real `<input type="file">` in the
   DOM and does not block anything.
3. `find` with a query like "hidden file input element" to get that input's ref
   (it only exists after step 2, there is none on the page before).
4. Call `file_upload` with that ref and the local file path. Drive's own "Uploading…"
   toast appears and the file lands in the current folder, confirmed by a green
   "upload complete" checkmark.
5. If step 2 or 3 ever stops finding the input (Google can change this), fall back to
   delivering the file to Martin with `SendUserFile` and naming the Drive folder, but
   try the steps above first — they are the real, working path, not a last resort.

**Learnings from the Dumann run (2026-10-11):**
- A multi-paragraph `type` action with blank lines between sections can trigger an
  early send after the first paragraph in this composer; the rest of the text then
  sits unsent in the box. Avoid blank lines in the typed message, or verify with a
  screenshot before sending.
- ChatGPT's chained "edit this image" follow-ups in the same thread (recognisable by
  "Interpreted the edit" appearing above the generation) have repeatedly stalled at
  95–98% and self-cancelled ("Image generation stopped"), even after "Try again". A
  fresh, complete, single-message generation in a new chat does not have this problem
  and should be preferred over iterative follow-ups.
- A very long prompt (about 12,000 characters, whole page copy) typed with the `type` action makes the page busy for about 1 to 2 minutes, and the tool reports a timeout and screenshots fail meanwhile. The typing still completes. Wait, then check with `javascript_tool` that the composer text length equals the prompt length and ends with the last words (`document.querySelector('#prompt-textarea').innerText`). Then find the Send button with `find` and click it. Do not retype.
- **Fast prompt insertion (2026-10-10, tested):** write the prompt to a file, run `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 pbcopy < prompt.txt`, click the composer, press `cmd+v`. ChatGPT turns a long paste (about 15,000 characters) into a chip "Pasted text" within seconds, no freeze. Click "Show in text field" on the chip, then check the length with `javascript_tool` (`document.querySelector('#prompt-textarea').innerText.length` must equal the file length), then find the Send button and click it. This replaces the slow `type` action.
- The "+" menu's "Add photos & files" item can trigger a native OS file picker that
  the agent cannot see or interact with; use the dedicated "Attach photos" file input
  instead, found fresh via `find` right before uploading (a stale element reference
  from an earlier screenshot can silently fail to attach).

**Build learnings (Dumann run, 2026-10-11):**
- Cut out portraits with the `rembg` Python API (`new_session('u2net')`, `alpha_matting=True`), not the `rembg` command line, which fails on a missing `watchdog` module. Run it with the Python that has `rembg` installed (`/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.10/bin/python3` on this Mac).
- Cut an icon sheet apart by labelling the non-white regions (scipy). Make the white background transparent by flood fill from the border, then blur the alpha by 1 px. A white box shows around icons on white cards otherwise.
- A line drawing on a solid purple image goes onto a band of nearly the same purple with `mix-blend-mode: lighten`. Do not use `screen`, it brightens the whole rectangle.
- A real photo cut out at the image edge shows a hard edge. Fade that side with a CSS `mask-image` gradient.
- A cutout has a pale fringe from the old backdrop. Fix it by edge unmixing: for every semi-transparent pixel, subtract the known backdrop colour (taken from the nearest fully transparent pixel of the source photo) and divide by the alpha. Do not fill edge pixels with the nearest solid colour: that makes blocky hair. Check the result on the real band colour at 100 percent.
- Always set `height:auto` on an `<img>` that has `width:100%` in CSS. A leftover `height` attribute stretches the picture (found on the about portrait; measured by M4b).
- Turn automatic hyphenation off in narrow cards (`hyphens:manual`). For one unavoidable long German word add a soft hyphen (`­`) at the compound break.
- A portrait on a 3:2 card is cropped from the top of the original, with the hairline visible. Check the crop at card size.
- Serve the folder with `python3 -m http.server <port>` for the live check. Port 8765 can be taken by an older process. Check with `curl` first.

**Build learnings (law firm run, 2026-10-10):**
- Chrome's real viewport is about 1440×757 (sometimes 1421×701 with scrollbar). The first screen must hold H1, one proof line and the CTA at **701 px height**. Put the rating line between the sub-headline and the buttons so proof and CTA are visible together. Check `getBoundingClientRect().bottom` of the CTA.
- A hero with three buttons or a long label wraps in a 700 px column. Use `flex-wrap:nowrap`, drop the arrow icon in the hero button and set padding to 24 px.
- `text-wrap: balance` on all headings removes single-word last lines.
- A fixed side rail with dark buttons vanishes on a dark band. Give the buttons a 2 px ring in the page colour.
- A "grey to ink while scrolling" paragraph: wrap each word, lighten words with `opacity` as a function of scroll position, never darken them again. Make the formula reach 100 percent while the paragraph is still well inside the screen.
- A hand-drawn wave under a headline line: a `::after` with a repeating SVG background, `transform: scaleX(0)` to `1` once on load. `white-space:nowrap` on the line, otherwise the wave stretches over the wrapped box.
- Numbers of the type 01, 02, 03 in stacked service rows keep links on one line when the item is a flex column and the link has `margin-top:auto`.
- Text check by script (M11): parse the HTML text nodes, normalise, and test each against the normalised `approved-copy.md`. Expect only the prototype notice to differ.

## Summary: Dumann CRO work in `/Users/martindrendel/741website`

### 1. Where it lives

There are **three separate CRO runs** for Dumann, all under `00_project/assets/dumann/` (none are committed to git — the whole `00_project/assets/dumann/` tree is untracked/new to git, `git status` shows `?? 00_project/assets/dumann/`):

| Run | Path | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **Homepage (Track A)** | `00_project/assets/dumann/cro/` | Standard CRO homepage workflow (matches the `meandyou/cro/lp-overlooked` structure) |

There is no separate `dumann-client.md`-referenced single canonical "cro" folder beyond these three; `00_project/assets/dumann/content-pool/` is a different workflow (SEO page-content / page-optimizer work for the live Wix site, not CRO).

### 2. Client info / website

- Steps 0–6b done, self-check score **39/42** (started at 11/42).

Memory file confirms: "Prototyp fertig... Handoff geschrieben, Status Übergeben, Freigabe durch Martin und Kundin offen" — i.e. handed off, now waiting on approval from both Martin and the client.

`git log --all --oneline -i --grep=dumann` only turns up commits about the **live site page content** (Startseite/Hildegard-Fasten/layout-QA/cache-buster fixes under `04_site`/`.preview-tmp`), e.g.:

```
4268fc5 Dumann: bump cache-buster after layout fix deploy
5308d6e Dumann: fix approval-button/heading overlap + cramped price tables
ae2b646 Dumann: rebuild all 6 pages with real client CI, not 741-report style
36880d1 Dumann: B3 Hildegard-Fasten page live, following corrected QA process
```
`git log -- 00_project/assets/dumann/cro` and `cro-b` return **nothing** — these CRO working folders were never committed to git at all (they're local/untracked working directories, likely meant for Drive export rather than git).

### 5. Reference structure (meandyou `cro/lp-overlooked`, for comparison)

Full stage folders used by a completed Track-A run:
```
00-lead-info.md
01-input/                (INVENTORY.md, source images)
02-data/brand.md, dataset.md, screenshots
03-diagnosis/diagnosis.md
04-copy/copy.md, gates.md, OPEN-FLAGS.md, approved-copy.md, approved-copy-plain.txt
05-gpt-design-doc/design-doc.md, prompt.txt, build_prompt.py, make_units.py, units.json, refs/
06-gpt-assets/full-page-v1-final.png, images/
07-prototype/index.html, build.py, assets/, screenshots/, self-check.md, visual-check.md
08-handoff/handoff.md
_status.md                (checkpoint/progress log, one line per step)
_drive/                   (flattened mirror of every stage file, for Google Drive sync, + MANIFEST.json + _status.md)
```
Checkpoint gates in this workflow are: **Checkpoint 1** = copy approval (after step 3/04-copy), **Checkpoint 2** = prototype + visual-check approval (after step 6/6b, before 07/08). A run is "done" when `08-handoff/handoff.md` exists and `_drive/` has been populated/mirrored (`_status.md` ends with a line referencing Drive upload or "fertig"/handoff).

Dumann's Track A homepage run (`cro/`) matches this structure almost exactly through step 6b but is missing `_drive/` entirely and has an empty `08-handoff/` — it is stalled at Checkpoint 2, waiting on Martin's decision on two copy items before the handoff/Drive step can run. The `ueber-mich/` sub-run and the Track B `cro-b/` run both got further (handoff written; Track B also has Drive mirror done).

# Self-Check v2: Prototyp Desktop 1440 px, Naturheilpraxis Daniela Dumann

Stand 2026-10-11. Prototyp: `07-prototype/v2/index.html` (eine Datei, Assets in `assets/`). Screenshots in `screenshots/`. v1 (mobile-first) bleibt unverändert in `07-prototype/`.

Geprüft in: Headless Chrome mit 1440 px Fensterbreite (`?shot=1` zeigt alle Reveal-Zustände) und Live-Scroll-Check in Martins Chrome: 28 Reveal-Elemente, alle werden einmalig sichtbar, keine kaputten Bilder, keine Konsolenfehler, Karte und Pin laden, CTA im ersten Bildschirm (Button endet bei y≈537 von 800).

Mobile ist nicht Teil dieses Workflows (Martin, 2026-10-11). Die Seite ist ab 1100 px Breite ausgelegt.

## Was neu ist gegenüber v1

- Layout Abschnitt für Abschnitt am finalen Mockup ausgerichtet: Kopfzeile mit sieben Menüpunkten, Hero mit Schmetterlings-Hintergrund und freigestelltem Portrait, Beweis-Leiste, fünf Themenkarten mit gemalten Icons, Leistungskarten, vier Schritte, dunkles Über-mich-Band mit Lavendel-Foto und Linienzeichnung, Bewertungen, FAQ, Standort mit Symbolen, Abschluss mit Linienzeichnungen links und rechts.
- Bilder: echte Portraits in voller Auflösung (freigestellt per rembg), echte Fotos von ihrer Website (Schmetterling, Lavendel, Fläschchen), sechs neu erzeugte Bilder in 1024 px oder mehr. Keine Ausschnitte aus dem Mockup mehr.
- Mobile-Teile entfernt: Sticky-Leiste, Telefon-Symbol im Kopf, Mobil-Breakpoints.

## Scorecard (Desktop)

| # | Item | Prio | Score | Beleg |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | Primärer CTA im ersten Bildschirm (1440×800) | A | 2 | Button bei y≈485–537 im Screenshot `desktop-1440-first-viewport.png` |
| 11 | CTA mindestens alle 2 Sektionen | A | 2 | Hero, Themen, Schritte, Über mich, Standort, Abschluss |
| 21 | Typografie | C | 2 | Body 17 px, Buttons 54 px |
| übrige | wie in `../self-check.md` (v1) | | | Inhalt unverändert, nur Layout und Bilder |

Summe unverändert 38 von 44. Zwei A-Items stehen weiter auf 1 und warten auf Martin: Item 3 (Sub-Headline Situation zuerst) und Item 5 (CTA-Text mit Nutzen). Item 6: die Zeile „Erstgespräch: 60 Minuten, 220 €" im Hero ist weiter nicht im freigegebenen Hero-Text.

## Abweichungen vom Mockup (bewusst)

- Leistungen: 3 × 2 Karten statt 6 in einer Reihe, weil sechs Spalten bei 1440 px zu schmal für die Überschriften sind.
- Karten-Schaltfläche: Textlink „Mehr erfahren" statt oliver Button, damit nur der Haupt-CTA oliv ist (Item 10).
- FAQ als Akkordeon, eine Antwort offen (Mockup zeigt alle offen).
- Kein Kopf-Button im Menü, wie im Mockup.
- Tagline „Naturheilkunde im Einklang mit Mensch und Natur" und die Pflanze im Standort-Abschnitt nicht übernommen.
- Bewegung nach `00_project/cro-homepage-motion-spec.md`: ein Highlight je Sektion, Breathing-CTA nur Hero und Abschluss.

## Offene Punkte (für Handoff)

- `[FEHLT]` Absage-/Stornobedingungen (Platzhalter im FAQ sichtbar markiert).
- `[FEHLT]` Parken am Standort.
- `[FEHLT]` Deutsche Originaltexte der Bewertungen.
- Shoot-Liste (erzeugte Bilder ersetzen durch echte Fotos): Darmsanierung, Ernährung, Homöopathie, Oligoscan, Massage. Das Icon-Set ist gemalt und bleibt.
- Leistungs-Links sind `#`-Platzhalter bis zum Rebuild.
- Karte lädt OpenStreetMap beim Aufruf, für den Live-Gang Einwilligung nötig (DSGVO).
- Impressum und Datenschutz sind Platzhalter. Das Logo-Icon (Hildegard-Zeichnung) ist nicht eingebaut.
- Mobile-Version: eigener späterer Workflow.
